paraphrase: Logical models and exclusions. Models of the bearer premises witness a terminus satisfying the substance predicate, a well-founded terminus failing it whose bearer has no bearer, a two-node cycle, an acyclic infinite chain, and a bundle whose members support each other while nothing bears the bundle. One bearer can have termini on both sides of the predicate, and a terminus together with a cycle. Without the ancestry premise a dependent bearer has no terminus in the nondependent sense. A terminus satisfying the predicate can be contingent. Omitting either subject-relation bridge leaves no terminus passing the Categories test; with both, a terminus passes it and can fail a separately supplied substance predicate. For every interpretation and bearer, each terminus form excludes the cycle and endless forms. No model is claimed metaphysically possible.
